title: Nu Skin India Partners with Akshaya Patra to Fund 700,000 School Meals
excerpt: The beauty and wellness company joins India's largest NGO-run school meal program to support mid-day meals for children in government schools.
body:
Nu Skin India, the Indian arm of Utah-based beauty and wellness company Nu Skin Enterprises (NYSE: NUS), has entered into a partnership with The Akshaya Patra Foundation to support 700,000 mid-day meals for children in government and government-aided schools, according to a press release published by the company.

The deal connects one of the world's largest direct-selling companies with India's biggest NGO-run school meal program, channeling corporate resources into a feeding infrastructure that already operates at massive scale.

A Global Mandate Meets Indian Scale

Nu Skin operates in nearly 50 markets worldwide and has built its philanthropic identity around the Nourish the Children initiative, launched in 2002. Through the program, the company's sales leaders, customers, and employees purchase and donate VitaMeal — a nutrient-dense food scientifically formulated by Nu Skin's nutritional scientists — to third-party charitable organizations for distribution.

The initiative reached a major milestone in May 2026, surpassing 900 million meals donated to malnourished children across more than 65 countries. The company currently feeds approximately 75,000 children daily through the program.

The India partnership marks a specific regional commitment within this broader global effort, directing support toward the country's established school meal infrastructure rather than VitaMeal distribution alone.

Akshaya Patra's Feeding Machine

The Akshaya Patra Foundation, headquartered in Bengaluru, has grown from serving 1,500 children in five schools in 2000 to feeding over 2.25 million children daily through 78 kitchen locations across 16 states and three union territories. The foundation operates as the primary NGO implementation partner of the Indian government's PM POSHAN Abhiyaan — formerly the National Programme for Mid-Day Meal in Schools — using a public-private partnership model.

"It is amazing to think of 900 million meals when you imagine the difference we have made in the lives of so many children around the world. And we're not done — we continue to feed 75,000 children each day as we set our sights on 1 billion meals."

— Ryan Napierski, President and CEO, Nu Skin Enterprises

The foundation's centralized kitchens use semi-automated cooking systems capable of preparing up to 104,000 meals per day at a single facility. Food is cooked under strict food safety management systems, packed into stainless steel containers, and transported via custom distribution vehicles to schools.

Akshaya Patra has cumulatively served over four billion meals since inception and has received significant recognition, including the Gandhi Peace Prize in 2016, the Nikkei Asia Prize, and the BBC Global Food Champion Award in 2019.

Corporate Partnerships Drive the Mission Forward

Nu Skin joins a growing list of international companies partnering with Akshaya Patra to fund school meals. Specialty chemicals firm Nouryon committed in 2025 to sponsor meals for 6,000 children over three years across locations from Dehradun to Bengaluru. Energy company BW LPG India has served as the foundation's energy partner since 2023, powering centralized kitchens with LPG across states including Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan. Mastercard has also collaborated with the foundation to provide millions of meals.

Each partnership functions on a cost-sharing model. The government provides a per-student allocation — historically around ₹1.75 per student — while corporate partners and individual donors cover the gap between the government subsidy and the actual cost of preparing a nutritious meal, which industry estimates place at ₹4.50 to ₹5 per student.

What This Means for the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, the mid-day meal program has long been a favored channel for charitable giving. Akshaya Patra operates dedicated international donation platforms, including through its UK entity, where NRI donors can contribute as little as £15 to feed a child for a year. The foundation's U.S. affiliate, Akshaya Patra USA, also facilitates tax-deductible donations.

Nu Skin's entry adds another corporate pathway for those looking to support school nutrition in India. The company's global network of brand affiliates and customers across nearly 50 markets could amplify awareness and fundraising for the cause beyond traditional donor channels.

Looking Ahead

The partnership comes as India's school meal infrastructure attracts international attention. Akshaya Patra has been exploring expansion of its model to Indonesia and Kenya, where governments are developing their own school feeding programs. Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto has launched a free school meal initiative partly inspired by India's mid-day meal scheme.

With Nu Skin setting a target of one billion cumulative meals globally, and Akshaya Patra aiming to reach three million children daily, the partnership reflects a convergence of corporate ambition and NGO scale in one of the world's most critical child nutrition programs.
